A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAREL framework. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support reliable comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendix A is available and included in this assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original BabyAI and SHELM experiments, including learning curves and instruction-tracking comparisons in Figures 2-3.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds benchmark comparisons, runtime measurements, and component ablations in the main text and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The core architecture, multi-grained contrastive objective, and instruction tracking are retained. However, the stated masking schedule changes from p = 0.8 tanh(2t/T) + 0.01 in v1 to p = tanh(t/T) in v2 Section 2.2.1, a limited procedural revision.

E1.justification: The five BabyAI levels and MiniGrid PutNear task are retained. v2 Figure 4 and Table 2 add RGB MiniGrid GoToObj and GoToDoor evaluations, extending task coverage within the existing gridworld domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds LISA as a comparator on GoToSeqS5R2 and OpenDoorsOrderN4 in Table 3. Figure 8 also adds BabyAI with instruction tracking but without CAREL as a control. The existing BabyAI and SHELM baselines remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces convergence-budget comparisons with LISA using 100,000 demonstration trajectories and a timing protocol averaging FPS over 100,000 frames. Plotted training horizons extend from 20M to 30M frames for Synth and from 5M to 10M for PutNear. These substantially expand the evaluation design.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's pooling and instruction-tracking comparisons, Appendix A.2 adds loss-coefficient sensitivity, action-embedding removal, alternative tracking similarity scores, and instruction tracking without CAREL. Appendix A.1 adds computational-cost analysis, substantially expanding component-level and supplementary evaluation.

E5.justification: Both versions state two random seeds and show shaded learning-curve bands. v2 additionally reports numerical ± terms in Tables 2-3, but does not define their statistical meaning or establish an increase in run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds LISA, additional MiniGrid, ablation, and runtime results, alongside revised learning curves. For example, Table 2 reports GoToDoor success of 83% ± 1% for SHELM + CAREL versus 50% ± 3% for SHELM at 1.5M frames. Table 4 newly reports average throughput of 420.17 FPS for CAREL versus 668.93 for BabyAI.

T1.justification: Equation 12 changes normalization from 1/n to 1/N, resolving the mismatch with the declared N-pair batch; n denotes episode length. Appendix A.4 also supplies a formal POMDP definition and discounted-return objective. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: auxiliary cross-modal alignment, instruction tracking, and improved sample efficiency and systematic generalization. Explicitly naming MiniGrid alongside BabyAI clarifies the existing two-benchmark scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explicit applicability discussion requiring textual instructions and modality embeddings. Appendix A.1 interprets the runtime penalty in relation to interaction efficiency, while A.2.3 explains the preference for episode-word similarity through its lower computational cost.

D1.justification: v2 documents conjunction-based parsing, replacement with mask tokens, and reward-threshold-based trajectory selection more explicitly. It also reports runtime estimates. Existing optimizer settings, learning rates, batch sizes, hardware, and code link are retained, with several settings relocated to Appendix A.

R1.justification: v2 adds Garg et al. on LISA, Yu on sample-efficient reinforcement learning, and Ladosz et al. on exploration. These support the new comparison and runtime discussion; the central positioning around adapting X-CLIP-style alignment to instruction-following RL remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Much of the original prose and overall narrative remains intact. v2 expands method motivation and worked instruction-tracking explanations, separates the pseudocode, reorganizes experimental subsections, and moves optimizer details into an appendix.

P2.justification: v2 introduces four tables and four appendix analysis figures, separates the SHELM comparison into an expanded three-panel Figure 4, and revises existing plot axes and captions. The document also adopts a substantially different journal layout, including wider text and figure placement.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.2 substantially strengthens component validation by isolating choices that v1 largely evaluated together. Runtime measurements expose the computational cost of sample-efficiency gains, and worked masking details improve reproducibility. These address important gaps in v1, although undefined uncertainty terms and unequal LISA training budgets limit the added comparative evidence.
